mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk-aversion and reduced liquidity in the equity market.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS drops below 5.25% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% followed by a stabilization signals disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggers, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not revert upward as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 2% above the prior month's level, sustained for two consecutive months, predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to rising labor costs and wage growth fears.
failure_condition: In regimes with strong wage growth, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the effect vanishes after adjusting for inflation proxies.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real private demand) grows at an annualized rate exceeding 4% for three consecutive quarters, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as market anticipates robust corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1_qt > prev_quarter + 4% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: Over 10 such expansion quarters, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or earnings growth decelerates sharply after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both INDPRO (industrial production) and HOUST (housing starts) by at least 2% month-over-month, lasting two months, predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it signals weakening economic momentum and investment caution.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev_month - 2% and HOUST < prev_month - 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 5 such events, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the two proxies revert upward before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as lower unemployment expectations reduce risk premia.
failure_condition: In regimes with falling labor costs, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only for short horizons.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) above 110% for two consecutive months, accompanied by FEDFUNDS < 1%, predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals excess liquidity supporting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 110 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: During such liquidity spikes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect disappears after controlling for inflation proxies.

mechanism_narrative: When a 3-month moving average of INDPRO falls below 100 (2017=100 baseline) and UNRATE remains above 4%, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent supply-side weakness and elevated unemployment.
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or UNRATE falls below 4% before the 60-day horizon.
